## Build your own content, and paint the menu your server's colour

The menu stops being only a way to play animations somebody else defined. An admin now places scenes in the world, in game, and picks the accent every player sees — neither one needs a file edit or a restart.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **The theme colours moved out of `config.lua`.**
>
> They ship in a new file, `default.lua`, and you change them **in game**: shield icon → Settings → pick a colour → Apply. It applies to everyone on the server at once and survives restarts.
>
> Your existing `config.lua` keeps working — it loads after `default.lua`, so anything you set there still wins. Nothing breaks on update. But the place to change colours from now on is the panel.
>
> `default.lua` is **ours**: an update overwrites it. `config.lua` is the file we never touch.

### Added: the scene editor

Walk to where an actor should stand, face the way they should face, press a key. That is the mark. No coordinates copied out of a dev tool, no Lua edited.

- **Spots** — one mark with an emote. Walk into it and a prompt offers the action: lean on the bar, address the podium, sit on the cell bunk. Your MLOs stop needing a board of `/e` commands taped to the wall.
- **Multi-actor scenes** — several marks, each with its own emote *and its own role name*. A wedding, an interrogation, a mugshot. Nearby players get a role card, walk to their mark, ready up, and everyone hits their pose on a shared countdown.
- **Built by you** — every server ends up with different scenes on different MLOs. This is not a fixed list of animations we picked.
- **Survives updates** — scenes live in your database, one row each, created automatically on first boot. There is no SQL file to import, and dropping a new version over the old one never touches your work.

### Added: the server's colour

Shield icon → Settings → a colour picker with a hex / `rgb()` field.

- It applies to **every player at once**, without a restart, and is remembered across them.
- **The whole UI follows it**, not just the highlights. Panels, cards and world prompts carry the accent's own hue at the lightness they already had, so amber turns the cards amber and a near-grey leaves them near-grey.
- It **tells you when a colour will not read** — a live contrast figure against the panel, flagged below 3:1. A warning, not a veto. It is your server.

### Added: Photo Mode Pro

- **A key light you place.** Positioned relative to the camera, so it keeps the same relationship to the shot however far you orbit — the difference between a photographic key light and a lamp someone left on. Front, side and rim are starting points; drag it anywhere.
- **Warmth on three real white points** — tungsten, daylight, open shade — rather than a hue shift, which is what makes it read as a lamp and not a filter.
- **Hour and sky, for the photographer only.** The world changes for whoever holds the camera and for nobody else, and everything is handed back on exit.
- **Frame a group.** Right-drag slides the framing off yourself, so you can photograph the people beside you. Bounded on purpose: it stays a camera rather than becoming a free one.

### Added: the admin menu

The shield in the header opens a small menu — *Scene editor* or *Settings*. The version, the update notice and the diagnostics live under Settings, where you look for them once and then never again.

Everything behind it is gated by one ACE permission, server-side. A player without it never receives the data at all, so there is nothing to hide in the client.

### Changed

- **Every surface in the UI derives from the accent.** Panels, cards and world prompts stopped being a fixed colour with a coloured highlight on top.
- **The world panels share one recipe** — the same gradient the emote wheel already used, so the pills, the scene cards and the editor bars finally read as one product.
- **Secondary text is lighter** (`8A93A6`): the old value measured 3.7:1 against the panel, below the readable threshold.
- **The settings popover is translated** in German, Spanish, French and Portuguese. Those 18 strings had been English inside an otherwise translated menu since the popover shipped.

### Fixed

- **Seat claims and scene sessions are resolved server-side.** They used to trust the client's own description of a scene, which let a modified client hold a seat it was nowhere near, and let a forged scene definition reach the people it invited.
- **Two admins saving a new scene at the same moment** no longer overwrite each other.
- **Invitations expire at the 30 seconds they advertise.** They used to sit on screen, blocking other prompts, until a separate one-minute sweep.
- **A prop preview cancelled mid-load** no longer leaves an object attached to nothing for the rest of the session.
- **The placing bar wraps** instead of letting its keys overlap the title on screens narrower than about 1500px.

### Install

1. Download `mbt_emote_menu.zip` below and replace your resource folder.
2. `ensure mbt_emote_menu` — or restart the server.

Requires [rpemotes-reborn](https://github.com/alberttheprince/rpemotes-reborn) **2.1.2 or newer**, unchanged from 1.7.0. The scene editor needs `oxmysql`; if it is missing the editor turns itself off and says so in console, and everything else keeps working.
